# Module — `tax-apportion`

The **decimal-DEPENDENT** billing slice: compute the apportioned tax on an amount
from a province's applicable rate, using Hydra's exact-integer tax math. Lifted from
`billing-system/src/hydra-api/massCredits/planning.ts` (`taxRateToMillionths`,
`computeApportionedTaxMinorUnits` — verbatim) plus the applicable-rate read used
across `src/rentsync-api/invoicing/taxes.ts`.

**This module has no `spec-codegen` block.** It is generated by the LLM path and
executes against a **disposable Postgres** substrate (`tools/pg-substrate.js`), NOT
the in-memory SQLite one — because its behaviour reads and returns the exact
`tax_rate` string (S4), and only Postgres returns `decimal` as an exact string.
Behavioural sources of truth:

- `standards/conventions.md` — S1 selection, S2 exact-decimal parsing, S3 half-up
  integer apportionment, S4 return shape + decimal fidelity, S5 access, S6 purity
- `contracts/tax-apportion.contract.md` — the exact signatures + the entity
- `constants.md` — scale, offset, regex, error message, ordering
- `fixtures/` — pure-math cases (rate/amount → cents, and ValidationError cases) and
  DB cases (seed rows, run, compare `{ taxRate, taxMinorUnits }`)
- `reference/tax-apportion.reference.ts` — the verbatim math + DB wrapper, the oracle

## Functions

- `computeApportionedTaxMinorUnits(amountMinorUnits, taxRate)` — S2 + S3 (pure).
- `computeApportionedProvincialTax(dataSource, date, provinceId, amountMinorUnits)`
  — S1 + S4 (DB).

## Acceptance

Valid iff every fixture passes: pure-math fixtures (exact `expect` and `throws`
for `ValidationError`) run with no DB; DB fixtures seed `TaxByProvince`, run
`computeApportionedProvincialTax`, and compare the full result `{ taxRate,
taxMinorUnits }` — `taxRate` **included** and compared as an exact string, which is
the whole point of the Postgres substrate. `tools/behavioral-diff.js` sweeps many
rates × amounts (pure) and many seeded DB states × queries (DB) against the verbatim
reference. `tools/pg-decimal-probe.js` separately confirms the decimal reads back as
its exact string on Postgres (the SQLite lie from `hydra-tax-lookup/tools/probe.js`
does not occur here).

## Why this needs Postgres (and the SQLite slice did not)

`hydra-tax-lookup` proved a decimal-FREE selection on in-memory SQLite and had to
**exclude** `tax_rate` from its oracle, because SQLite returns `decimal` as a lossy
JS number. This slice's result **is** the rate (as an exact string) and a value
computed from it, so SQLite cannot host it honestly. Real Postgres returns
`tax_rate` as its exact scale-preserved string, so the rate is compared directly and
the arithmetic is exact. This is the hybrid: route decimal-free logic to SQLite,
decimal-dependent logic to Postgres.

## Assumptions

- **Well-formed arguments.** An initialised `DataSource` with the entity registered,
  an ISO `date`, an integer `provinceId`, and an integer `amountMinorUnits`.
  Malformed top-level arguments are out of scope and unguarded (contract).
- **Rate strings are non-negative decimals.** DB `tax_rate` values are plain
  non-negative decimals; a value that is not (e.g. a negative) makes
  `taxRateToMillionths` throw `ValidationError` (S2) — covered by a fixture.
- **`memoize` is not part of behaviour.** The source memoises reads; caching does
  not change the result.
- **Execution** — the generated `.ts` runs under Node's native type-stripping via
  the substrate; it uses only TypeORM's runtime API and language built-ins (S6).
